answer: Give every identity a slow-growing, non-transferable reputation score stored in a tamper-evident vault: a newcomer earns points only by completing independently verified useful tasks over several weeks, and points decay when idle. Splitting work across many fake identities is self-defeating because rewards scale sublinearly with score, so one seasoned identity out-earns a nebula of fresh clones. Attackers face a real cost - weeks of verified labour per identity, like growing timber rather than printing it - while honest agents keep their standing by doing ordinary work.
